name: Chicken Dhansak
blurb: Sweet-and-sour lentil curry with chicken, pumpkin and a hint of pineapple.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin
method: Fry the onion until golden, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the lentils, pumpkin and 700ml water and simmer 20 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and cook 15 minutes.
Stir in tamarind and sugar, blitz half for body, finish with coriander.

name: Beef Massaman Curry
blurb: Mild, rich Thai curry with slow beef, potatoes, peanuts and warm spice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tbsp tamarind
method: Fry the paste in the thick coconut cream with the whole spices for 2 minutes.
Add the beef to coat, then the rest of the coconut milk and 300ml water. Simmer 1.5 hours.
Add the potatoes, onion and peanuts and cook 30 minutes until the beef is tender.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and tamarind; serve with rice.

name: Panang Chicken Curry
blurb: A thick, nutty, slightly sweet red curry with kaffir lime.
ingredients: 3 tbsp panang or red curry paste
2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp palm sugar
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the chicken to coat, then the coconut milk and peanut butter.
Simmer 12 minutes, adding the lime leaves.
Season with fish sauce and sugar; finish with Thai basil.

name: Goan Pork Vindaloo
blurb: Fiery, vinegar-sharp pork curry with plenty of chilli and garlic.
ingredients: Marinade: 6 dried Kashmiri chillies, 8 garlic cloves, 3cm ginger, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp black pepper, 4 cloves, 1 tsp cinnamon, 5 tbsp red wine vinegar
method: Blitz the marinade to a paste and coat the pork; leave 2 hours.
Fry the onions until deep golden.
Add the pork and marinade and brown, then add 300ml water.
Cover and simmer 1 hour until tender; balance with the sugar.

name: Thai Red Prawn Curry
blurb: Coconut red curry with prawns, peppers and bamboo shoots.
ingredients: 2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, juice of 1 lime
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, pepper and bamboo and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes until pink.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime; finish with basil.

name: Chicken Korma
blurb: Very mild, sweet and creamy with cashew, coconut and cardamom.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cardamom, cumin, coriander, 1/2 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the onion until soft, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the chicken and brown lightly.
Add the cashew paste, cream and coconut milk and simmer gently 20 minutes.
Balance with the sugar; serve with rice or naan.

name: Egg Masala
blurb: Boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy.
ingredients: 1 tsp each turmeric, cumin, coriander, chilli powder
method: Rub the peeled eggs with turmeric and salt and fry until blistered.
Fry the onions until golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a thick masala, then 250ml water and simmer 8 minutes.
Return the eggs, finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: Chickpea & Spinach Curry (Chana Saag)
blurb: Chickpeas and spinach in a quick, spiced tomato sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli
method: Fry the onion until golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook down 8 minutes.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few.
Stir through the spinach and garam masala.

name: Keralan Fish Molee
blurb: White fish poached gently in a mild turmeric-coconut sauce with curry leaves.
ingredients: 600g firm white fish, in large pieces
1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig of curry leaves
400ml coconut milk, juice of half a lime
method: Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, then the onion until soft.
Add garlic, ginger, chilli and turmeric.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes.
Slip in the fish and poach 6-8 minutes; finish with lime.

name: Lamb Saag
blurb: Tender lamb in a silky spiced spinach sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp each cumin, coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder
method: Brown the lamb, then set aside. Fry the onions until golden, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Return the lamb, stir in the yoghurt a spoon at a time, add 200ml water. Simmer 1.5 hours.
Wilt the spinach with a splash of water and blitz to a purée.
Stir the spinach into the lamb and simmer 15 minutes; finish with garam masala.

name: Thai Yellow Vegetable Curry
blurb: A gentle turmeric-yellow coconut curry with mixed vegetables and tofu.
ingredients: 2 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, juice of 1 lime
method: Fry the tofu in oil until golden; set aside.
Fry the paste in a little coconut cream, add the rest with 200ml water.
Add the sweet potato and simmer 10 minutes, then the pepper and beans for 5.
Return the tofu, season with soy, sugar and lime; finish with coriander.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
blurb: Soft paneer in a mild, buttery, tomato-cream makhani sauce.
ingredients: 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp dried fenugreek
method: Fry the paneer in a little butter until golden; set aside.
Melt the butter, fry the onion, then garlic and ginger.
Add the blitzed tomatoes, chilli powder and sugar and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the cream, fenugreek, garam masala and paneer and simmer 5 minutes.

name: Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
blurb: Dark-roasted curry spices, coconut, curry leaf, pandan and lime.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Sri Lankan roasted curry powder
1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig curry leaves, 1 cinnamon stick
method: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp curry powder, salt and pepper.
Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, cinnamon and onion until soft.
Add garlic, ginger, the rest of the curry powder and the tomatoes.
Add the chicken, coconut milk and tamarind, cover and simmer 35 minutes.

name: Aloo Matar (Potato & Pea Curry)
blurb: Potatoes and peas in a simple, homely spiced tomato gravy.
ingredients: 1 tsp each turmeric, coriander, chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the cumin seeds, then the onion until golden.
Add garlic, ginger and ground spices, then the tomatoes and cook to a paste.
Add the potatoes and 300ml water and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the peas for the last 5 minutes; finish with garam masala.

name: Beef Rendang
blurb: Malaysian dry curry — beef slow-cooked in coconut and spice until dark and sticky.
ingredients: Paste: 6 shallots, 6 garlic cloves, 4cm ginger, 3cm galangal, 2 lemongrass, 6 dried chillies
1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 3 star anise, 4 lime leaves
method: Blitz the paste and fry in oil with the whole spices until fragrant.
Add the beef to coat, then the coconut milk and lime leaves.
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, for 2-2.5 hours until the liquid has cooked off and the beef is dark.
Stir in the toasted coconut, tamarind and sugar for the last 15 minutes.

name: Tarka Dal
blurb: Yellow lentils cooked soft and finished with a sizzling spiced ghee.
ingredients: Tarka: 3 tbsp ghee or oil, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 4 garlic cloves sliced, 1 dried red chilli, pinch of asafoetida
method: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and 1 litre water for 25-30 minutes; whisk to a loose porridge and season.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin, then the garlic until pale gold.
Add the dried chilli, asafoetida, tomato and chilli powder and fry 2 minutes.
Pour the tarka over the dal and finish with coriander and lemon.

name: Everyday Chicken Curry
blurb: The reliable, medium-spiced tomato-and-onion chicken curry for any night.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli
method: Fry the onions until deep golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook down 8 minutes.
Add the chicken and 200ml water and simmer 20 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: South Indian Prawn Coconut Curry
blurb: Prawns in a tangy, chilli-flecked coconut sauce with curry leaves.
ingredients: 1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig curry leaves
1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric
method: Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, then the onion.
Add garlic, ginger, chilli powder and turmeric, then the tomatoes.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes until pink.

name: Thai Jungle Curry (Gaeng Pa)
blurb: A fiery, brothy curry with no coconut — just chilli, herbs and vegetables.
ingredients: 3 tbsp jungle or red curry paste
150g green beans, 1 courgette, 100g baby corn, 1 bamboo tin
2 tbsp fish sauce, handful of Thai basil and green peppercorns
method: Fry the paste in a little oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken to coat, then the stock.
Add the vegetables and simmer 8 minutes.
Season with fish sauce; finish with basil and peppercorns.

name: Chicken Chettinad
blurb: Peppery, roasted-spice South Indian curry with plenty of black pepper.
ingredients: Spice roast: 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tbsp black pepper, 1 tsp fennel, 4 dried chillies, 3 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 tbsp desiccated coconut
method: Dry-roast the spice mix until fragrant, then grind.
Fry the onions until golden with curry leaves, add garlic and ginger.
Add the ground spice mix and tomatoes and cook to a paste.
Add the chicken and 200ml water, cover and simmer 30 minutes.

name: Sweet Potato & Lentil Curry
blurb: Red lentils and sweet potato simmered soft with coconut and warm spice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric
150g spinach, juice of half a lime
method: Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the lentils, sweet potato, coconut milk, tomatoes and 300ml water.
Simmer 25 minutes until the lentils collapse and the potato is soft.
Stir through the spinach and lime.

name: Methi Chicken (Chicken with Fenugreek)
blurb: A medium curry with a distinctive slightly bitter, aromatic fenugreek note.
ingredients: 1 tsp each turmeric, cumin, coriander, chilli
method: Fry the onions until golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a paste, then stir in the yoghurt.
Add the chicken and 150ml water and simmer 20 minutes.
Crush in the fenugreek and add garam masala for the last 5 minutes.

name: Sweet Potato Katsu Curry
blurb: Panko sweet potato slabs with a mild Japanese curry sauce and rice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp garam masala
500ml vegetable stock, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp maple
method: Steam the sweet potato slabs for 6 minutes until just tender; cool.
Soften the onion and carrot, add garlic, ginger and spices, then the flour.
Whisk in the stock, soy and maple; simmer 15 minutes and blitz smooth.
Coat the slabs in flour, milk and panko and shallow fry until golden; serve with rice and sauce.

name: Lamb Keema Pav
blurb: Buttery toasted rolls with rich spiced lamb mince and peas.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the cumin seeds, then the onion until golden; add garlic and ginger.
Add the mince and brown, then the ground spices and tomatoes; cook 8 minutes.
Add 150ml water and simmer 10 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5.
Toast buttered rolls in a pan and serve alongside the keema to scoop.
